intro: Welcome to B2! You already tell stories with the past simple, the past continuous and the past perfect. Now you'll choose each tense on purpose, add the past perfect continuous (I had been waiting for two hours when she finally arrived), and talk about old habits with would and used to.
teachingNotes: Builds on: past simple vs past continuous with when/while (b1-past-continuous), the past perfect had + third form for the earlier event, with when/by the time (b1-past-perfect), have/has been + -ing with for/since/How long and the simple-vs-continuous choice (b1-present-perfect-continuous), used to for past habits and states (b1-used-to), and the shape of a story with suddenly/in the end (b1-telling-stories). Recap each in one line; don't re-teach the forms.

Combining the tenses: the new B2 skill is choosing deliberately. Past continuous = in the middle of something at that moment (the scene); past simple = the events, in order (or something that happened at that exact moment); past perfect = already finished before that moment. Key contrast: When I got to the platform, the train was leaving (I saw it go) / left (at that moment) / had left (it was gone). Indonesian verbs don't change and sedang/sudah are often dropped, so check every verb. Common error: *'When I arrived, the film already started' → 'had already started' (sudah in a past story → had). Informal American English sometimes uses already + past simple (I already ate); accept it in free speech if asked, but in past stories this course expects had. Don't overuse had: one event, or events in order, stay in the past simple; had is for going back. After realised / remembered / noticed / found out, had + third form is very common.

Past perfect continuous: had been + -ing, the same for every person, short form 'd been. Use: an activity in progress for a while up to a moment in the past (often with for / since / all day / How long), or the reason for something that could be seen then (The streets were wet. It had been raining.). It is the past version of I've been waiting (up to now) → I had been waiting (up to then). Common error: *'I waited for two hours when she finally came' → 'I had been waiting for two hours when she finally came'; also *'I was waiting for two hours when…' (the past continuous can't show how long up to that moment, like *'I am waiting for an hour'). 'I had waited for two hours when…' is also possible English: accept it, never make had waited vs had been waiting an either-or question.

Simple vs continuous in the past perfect, test only clear cases: a number or a finished result → had + third form (By noon she had answered 40 emails, not *had been answering 40 emails); the activity / its length / a visible result → had been + -ing. State verbs (know, have = own, like, believe, understand, be) stay simple: I had known him for ten years (not *had been knowing). With live, work, study and teach + for/since both forms are fine: never mark one wrong.

would vs used to for past habits: used to + base verb = past habits AND past states. would + base verb = only repeated ACTIONS in the past, mostly in memory stories, and only after the time is set (When I was a kid, … / Every Sunday, …): When I was a kid, my dad would take me to the market every Sunday. Never for states: *'I would have a bike' → 'I used to have a bike'; same for live, like, know, be. Not for one single event (past simple). would for habits is rare in negatives and questions: use didn't use to / Did you use to …? Indonesian learners know would as 'akan' / 'mau' (would like, second conditional): here it means 'dulu biasanya'. 'd + base verb = would (we'd play); 'd + third form = had (we'd played). Test only state verbs (have, live, like, know, be) vs actions; where both would and used to fit, never make them an either-or question. The past simple is also always correct for past habits and states.

Limits: no third conditional (if I had known), no past modals (must have been), no passive beyond present/past simple, no reported speech with tense changes, no future perfect, no participle clauses. Keep sentences adult and Indonesian (KRL, ojek, office, campus, weddings, mudik) and explanations in plain Indonesian with 'kamu'.

keyPoints.title: Three past tenses, chosen on purpose
keyPoints.explanation: In a story, the past continuous (was/were + -ing) is the scene: something in the middle of happening at that moment. The past simple tells the events, in order. The past perfect (had + third form) goes back to something already finished before that moment. The same verb tells three different stories: When I got to the platform, the train was leaving (I saw it go) / left (at that moment) / had left (it was already gone). Indonesian 'sudah' in a past story → had: the film had already started (not 'already started').

examples.en: When I got to the platform, the train was leaving.
examples.id: Waktu saya sampai di peron, keretanya sedang berangkat.

examples.en: When I got to the platform, the train had left.
examples.id: Waktu saya sampai di peron, keretanya sudah berangkat.

examples.en: Suddenly I realised that I had left my laptop at the office.
examples.id: Tiba-tiba saya sadar laptop saya tertinggal di kantor.

id.title: Tiga past tense, dipilih dengan sengaja
id.explanation: Dalam cerita, past continuous (was/were + -ing) adalah latarnya: sesuatu yang sedang berlangsung pada saat itu. Past simple menceritakan kejadiannya, sesuai urutan. Past perfect (had + bentuk ketiga) kembali ke sesuatu yang sudah selesai sebelum saat itu. Kata kerja yang sama bisa menceritakan tiga hal berbeda: When I got to the platform, the train was leaving (saya melihatnya pergi) / left (tepat saat itu) / had left (keretanya sudah tidak ada). 'sudah' dalam cerita lampau → had: the film had already started (bukan 'already started').

keyPoints.title: had been + -ing: in progress up to a past moment
keyPoints.explanation: The past perfect continuous (had been + -ing) is for an activity that was going on for a while up to a moment in the past: I had been waiting for two hours when she finally arrived. It's the past version of I've been waiting (up to now). Not 'I waited for two hours when she came' or 'I was waiting for two hours when she came'. It also explains something you could see then: The streets were wet. It had been raining. For a number or a finished result, use had + third form: By noon she had answered 40 emails. State verbs stay simple: I had known him for years.

examples.en: I had been waiting for two hours when she finally arrived.
examples.id: Saya sudah menunggu dua jam waktu dia akhirnya datang.

examples.en: The streets were wet. It had been raining.
By noon she had answered 40 emails.
examples.id: Sampai jam 12 siang dia sudah membalas 40 email.

id.title: had been + -ing: berlangsung sampai suatu saat di masa lalu
id.explanation: Past perfect continuous (had been + -ing) dipakai untuk kegiatan yang sudah berlangsung beberapa lama sampai suatu saat di masa lalu: I had been waiting for two hours when she finally arrived. Ini versi lampau dari I've been waiting (sampai sekarang). Bukan 'I waited for two hours when she came' atau 'I was waiting for two hours when she came'. Bentuk ini juga menjelaskan sesuatu yang terlihat saat itu: The streets were wet. It had been raining. Untuk jumlah atau hasil yang sudah selesai, pakai had + bentuk ketiga: By noon she had answered 40 emails. Kata kerja keadaan tetap simple: I had known him for years.

keyPoints.title: would and used to for old habits
keyPoints.explanation: used to + base verb is for past habits AND past states: I used to have a bike. I used to take the KRL. would + base verb is only for repeated actions in the past, usually in a memory story after the time is set: When I was a kid, my dad would take me to the market every Sunday. Never use would for states (have, live, like, know, be): 'I would have a bike' ✗ → I used to have a bike ✓. Here would means 'dulu biasanya', not 'akan'.

examples.en: When I was a kid, I used to have a bike.
examples.id: Waktu kecil, saya dulu punya sepeda.

examples.en: When I was a kid, my dad would take me to the market every Sunday.
examples.id: Waktu saya kecil, ayah dulu biasa mengajak saya ke pasar setiap Minggu.

examples.en: We used to live in Bogor.
examples.id: Dulu kami tinggal di Bogor. (keadaan: bukan would)

id.title: would dan used to untuk kebiasaan lama
id.explanation: used to + kata kerja dasar dipakai untuk kebiasaan lampau DAN keadaan lampau: I used to have a bike. I used to take the KRL. would + kata kerja dasar hanya untuk kegiatan yang berulang di masa lalu, biasanya dalam cerita kenangan setelah waktunya disebut dulu: When I was a kid, my dad would take me to the market every Sunday. Jangan pakai would untuk keadaan (have, live, like, know, be): 'I would have a bike' ✗ → I used to have a bike ✓. Di sini would artinya 'dulu biasanya', bukan 'akan'.

guidedPractice.hint: The band started before you arrived (you missed the first song) → the earlier event takes had + third form.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'eat' (past simple, past continuous or past perfect): When my boss called, I ___ lunch, so I answered with my mouth full.
guidedPractice.hint: Your mouth was full: you were in the middle of lunch at that moment → was/were + -ing.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the past perfect continuous of 'rain': The roads in Kemang were flooded because it ___ all night.
guidedPractice.hint: The flood is the result you could see; the rain went on for a long time before that → had been + -ing.

guidedPractice.prompt: Put the verb in the right form (had + third form or had been + -ing): By the end of the trip, we ___ (visit) six cities.
guidedPractice.hint: Six cities is a number of finished visits → had + third form, not had been + -ing.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with would or used to and the verb in brackets (only one is possible here): We ___ (have) a cat called Mochi when I was little.
guidedPractice.hint: have = own (punya) is a state, not a repeated action. would is only for repeated actions.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'cook' (past simple, past continuous or past perfect): The wedding was the next day. At 9 p.m. the electricity suddenly went off. At that moment, Bu Ani ___ rendang for 200 guests, so she carried the big pot to her neighbour's gas stove and finished it there.
acceptableAnswers: was cooking
was still cooking
assessment.rubric: Correct: was cooking (at that moment she was in the middle of cooking; the power cut interrupted it, and she finished later). 'had been cooking' = 70 (possible English, but 'at that moment' asks what was in progress then). 'cooked' = 30 (sounds like she started cooking after the power cut). 'had cooked' = 20 (it was already finished, but she finished it later). 'were cooking' = 60.

acceptableAnswers: when i got to my desk i saw that someone had already taken my chair
when i got to my desk i saw someone had already taken my chair
when i got to my desk i saw that someone had taken my chair
when i got to my desk i saw someone had taken my chair
when i got to my desk i noticed that someone had already taken my chair
when i got to my desk i noticed someone had already taken my chair
assessment.rubric: Correct: When I got to my desk, I saw that someone had (already) taken my chair (the chair was taken before I arrived: 'sudah' in a past story → had + third form). 'had already took' = 50 (the past form instead of the third form). 'has already taken' = 40. 'was taking' = 30 (that means it happened while I watched). Unchanged = 0. Missing comma: no penalty.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the past perfect continuous of 'try': Budi ___ to call the hotel all afternoon, so he was relieved when someone finally answered.
acceptableAnswers: had been trying
'd been trying
assessment.rubric: Correct: had been trying (an activity going on all afternoon, up to the moment someone answered). 'had tried' = 50 (correct English, but not the form asked for). 'was trying' = 40. 'has been trying' = 30 (that's up to now, not up to a past moment). 'had been try' = 50. 'had trying' = 30.

'had waited' = 60 (possible English, but the task asks for the past perfect continuous). 'were waiting' = 30 (the past continuous can't show how long up to that moment). 'have been waiting' = 30. Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Say it in English with the past perfect continuous. Start with 'Her eyes were red because…': Matanya merah, habis menangis.
acceptableAnswers: her eyes were red because she had been crying
her eyes were red because she'd been crying
assessment.rubric: Correct: Her eyes were red because she had been crying (the red eyes were the result you could see of an activity that had just stopped → had been + -ing). 'she was crying' = 40 (that means she was still crying at that moment). 'she has been crying' = 40 (the story is in the past). 'she cried' = 40. 'she had cried' = 50. 'she had been cry' = 60.

assessment.prompt: Complete with used to or would and the verb in brackets (only one is correct here): My brother ___ (be) really shy as a teenager, but now he's a TV presenter.
acceptableAnswers: used to be
assessment.rubric: Correct: used to be (be shy is a state, so would is impossible). 'would be' = 0 (would is only for repeated actions). 'was' = 70 (correct English, but the task asks for used to or would). 'use to be' = 60 (spelling: used to). 'used to being' = 40.

blocks.text:
Quick recap: you already know three past tenses for telling stories.
- **Past simple** (*went, stopped, realised*): the **events**, one after another. It moves the story forward.
- **Past continuous** (was/were + -ing: *was raining, were waiting*): the **scene**, something that was **in the middle** of happening at that moment.
- **Past perfect** (had + third form: *had left*): going **back** to something that was **already finished** before that moment.

The new B2 skill is to **choose on purpose**, because the same verb can tell three different stories:
- *When I got to the platform, the train **was leaving**.* → it was moving out as I arrived: I saw it go.
- *When I got to the platform, the train **left**.* → it left at that exact moment, just as I got there.
- *When I got to the platform, the train **had left**.* → it left before I arrived: the platform was empty.

For every verb in your story, ask: **at that moment, was it in the middle, did it happen right then, or was it already finished?**

id.text:
Ingat lagi: kamu sudah kenal tiga past tense untuk bercerita.
- **Past simple** (*went, stopped, realised*): **kejadian-kejadiannya**, satu demi satu. Bentuk ini menggerakkan cerita.
- **Past continuous** (was/were + -ing: *was raining, were waiting*): **latarnya**, sesuatu yang **sedang** berlangsung pada saat itu.
- **Past perfect** (had + bentuk ketiga: *had left*): **kembali** ke sesuatu yang **sudah selesai** sebelum saat itu.

Keterampilan baru di B2 adalah **memilih dengan sengaja**, karena kata kerja yang sama bisa menceritakan tiga hal berbeda:
- *When I got to the platform, the train **was leaving**.* → keretanya sedang bergerak pergi waktu saya sampai: saya melihatnya pergi.
- *When I got to the platform, the train **left**.* → keretanya berangkat tepat saat itu, persis waktu saya sampai.
- *When I got to the platform, the train **had left**.* → keretanya berangkat sebelum saya sampai: peronnya sudah kosong.

Untuk setiap kata kerja dalam ceritamu, tanyakan: **pada saat itu, apakah kegiatannya sedang berlangsung, terjadi tepat saat itu, atau sudah selesai?**

blocks.text:
Indonesian trap: Indonesian verbs don't change. *Keretanya berangkat* can mean any of the three, and *sedang* or *sudah* is often left out. English has to choose:
- *sedang* in a past story → **was/were + -ing**
- *sudah* in a past story → **had + third form**: *Waktu saya sampai, filmnya sudah mulai* → *When I arrived, the film **had already started*** (not *the film already started*). (In informal American English you may hear *I already ate*, but in a past story like this, use **had**.)

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: kata kerja bahasa Indonesia tidak berubah. *Keretanya berangkat* bisa berarti ketiganya, dan *sedang* atau *sudah* sering tidak diucapkan. Bahasa Inggris harus memilih:
- *sedang* dalam cerita lampau → **was/were + -ing**
- *sudah* dalam cerita lampau → **had + bentuk ketiga**: *Waktu saya sampai, filmnya sudah mulai* → *When I arrived, the film **had already started*** (bukan *the film already started*). (Dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika yang santai kamu mungkin mendengar *I already ate*, tapi dalam cerita lampau seperti ini, pakai **had**.)

blocks.prompt: Which sentence means the bus was already gone when Sari got to the bus stop?
options: When Sari got to the bus stop, the bus was leaving.
When Sari got to the bus stop, the bus had left.
When Sari got to the bus stop, the bus left.
blocks.explain: had left = the bus left first, before Sari arrived, so it was already gone. 'was leaving' = it was pulling away as she arrived, and 'left' = it left at that exact moment.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang berarti busnya sudah tidak ada waktu Sari sampai di halte?
id.explain: had left = busnya berangkat lebih dulu, sebelum Sari sampai, jadi busnya sudah tidak ada. 'was leaving' = busnya sedang bergerak pergi waktu dia sampai, dan 'left' = busnya berangkat tepat saat itu.

blocks.text:
A good story moves between the three tenses, and each verb has a reason. Read this one and look at why each tense is there:

*It was a Friday evening, and it **was raining**. The KRL **was packed**, and people **were pushing** to get on. I **squeezed** in, **found** a corner and **closed** my eyes. Suddenly I **realised** that I **had left** my laptop at the office. I **got off** at the next station and **went** back.*

- The **scene** (weather, the crowd, what was going on) → past continuous. (*was packed* is just *was* + an adjective: a description.)
- The **events**, in the order they happened → past simple.
- One step **back** in time (the laptop was left there earlier) → past perfect.

You don't need **had** for every verb: once you are telling events in order, the past simple is enough. Verbs like **realised, remembered, noticed, found out** (*menyadari, ingat, melihat, tahu*) are often followed by the past perfect, because you suddenly think of something that happened **before**.

id.text:
Cerita yang bagus berpindah-pindah di antara ketiga tense itu, dan setiap kata kerja punya alasan. Baca cerita ini dan perhatikan kenapa tiap tense dipakai:

*It was a Friday evening, and it **was raining**. The KRL **was packed**, and people **were pushing** to get on. I **squeezed** in, **found** a corner and **closed** my eyes. Suddenly I **realised** that I **had left** my laptop at the office. I **got off** at the next station and **went** back.*

- **Latar** (cuaca, keramaian, apa yang sedang terjadi) → past continuous. (*was packed* hanyalah *was* + kata sifat: sebuah gambaran.)
- **Kejadian-kejadiannya**, sesuai urutan → past simple.
- Satu langkah **mundur** dalam waktu (laptopnya tertinggal lebih dulu) → past perfect.

Tidak semua kata kerja perlu **had**: kalau kamu menceritakan kejadian sesuai urutan, past simple sudah cukup. Kata kerja seperti **realised, remembered, noticed, found out** (*menyadari, ingat, melihat, tahu*) sering diikuti past perfect, karena kamu tiba-tiba teringat sesuatu yang terjadi **sebelumnya**.

rows.note: the story moves on → past simple

blocks.text: Don't overuse **had**. One past event, or events told in order, stay in the past simple: *Last Saturday we **drove** to Bandung, **had** lunch and **came** back* (not *we had driven*). Use **had + third form** only when you jump **back** to something before the moment you are talking about.

id.text: Jangan berlebihan memakai **had**. Satu kejadian lampau, atau kejadian yang diceritakan sesuai urutan, tetap memakai past simple: *Last Saturday we **drove** to Bandung, **had** lunch and **came** back* (bukan *we had driven*). Pakai **had + bentuk ketiga** hanya kalau kamu melompat **mundur** ke sesuatu sebelum saat yang sedang kamu ceritakan.

blocks.prompt: I was walking to the office when I ___ that I had forgotten my ID card.
blocks.explain: realised is the short event that cuts into the walk → past simple. The forgetting happened earlier → had forgotten. 'had realised' would put the realising before the walk, and 'realise' isn't normally used in the -ing form.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: I was walking to the office when I ___ that I had forgotten my ID card.
id.explain: realised adalah kejadian singkat yang memotong kegiatan berjalan → past simple. Lupanya terjadi lebih dulu → had forgotten. 'had realised' membuat sadarnya terjadi sebelum berjalan, dan 'realise' biasanya tidak dipakai dalam bentuk -ing.

id.title: Satu cerita, setiap kata kerja dipilih

material.title: had been + -ing: in progress up to a past moment

blocks.text:
The **past perfect continuous** is **had been + -ing**: *I **had been waiting**. She **had been working**.* It's the same for every person (I, she, they **had been**), and the short form is **'d been**: *We'd been driving for hours.*

Use it for an activity that was **going on for a while up to a moment in the past**. It's simply the past version of the present perfect continuous you know:
- *I've been waiting for an hour.* → up to **now** (I'm still here).
- *I **had been waiting** for an hour **when** she called.* → up to **then** (the moment she called).

It often comes with **for** (a length of time), **since** (a starting point), **all day / all morning**, or **How long …?**: *How long **had** you **been living** in Surabaya when you met Dimas?*

Why not the past continuous? *I was waiting when she called* is correct, but it only says you were in the middle of waiting. It can't say **how long**. To add *for two hours*, you need **had been waiting**, just like *I am waiting for an hour* ✗ → *I've been waiting for an hour* ✓.

id.text:
**Past perfect continuous** adalah **had been + -ing**: *I **had been waiting**. She **had been working**.* Bentuknya sama untuk semua orang (I, she, they **had been**), dan bentuk pendeknya **'d been**: *We'd been driving for hours.*

Pakai bentuk ini untuk kegiatan yang **sudah berlangsung beberapa lama sampai suatu saat di masa lalu**. Ini hanyalah versi lampau dari present perfect continuous yang sudah kamu kenal:
- *I've been waiting for an hour.* → sampai **sekarang** (saya masih di sini).
- *I **had been waiting** for an hour **when** she called.* → sampai **saat itu** (saat dia menelepon).

Bentuk ini sering muncul dengan **for** (lamanya waktu), **since** (titik awal), **all day / all morning** (seharian / sepanjang pagi), atau **How long …?**: *How long **had** you **been living** in Surabaya when you met Dimas?*

Kenapa bukan past continuous? *I was waiting when she called* itu benar, tapi hanya mengatakan kamu sedang menunggu. Kalimat itu tidak bisa mengatakan **berapa lama**. Untuk menambahkan *for two hours*, kamu perlu **had been waiting**, sama seperti *I am waiting for an hour* ✗ → *I've been waiting for an hour* ✓.

rows.en: I had been waiting for two hours when she finally arrived.
rows.id: Saya sudah menunggu dua jam waktu dia akhirnya datang.
rows.note: two hours, up to the moment she arrived

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: *Saya sudah menunggu dua jam waktu dia datang.* Many learners say *I **waited** for two hours when she came* or *I **was waiting** for two hours when she came*. Both sound wrong in English. The waiting went on **up to** the moment she came → **I had been waiting for two hours when she came.** (*I had waited for two hours* is also possible, but the continuous is the natural choice for a wait.)

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *Saya sudah menunggu dua jam waktu dia datang.* Banyak pelajar mengatakan *I **waited** for two hours when she came* atau *I **was waiting** for two hours when she came*. Keduanya terdengar salah dalam bahasa Inggris. Menunggunya berlangsung **sampai** saat dia datang → **I had been waiting for two hours when she came.** (*I had waited for two hours* juga mungkin, tapi bentuk continuous adalah pilihan yang wajar untuk menunggu.)

blocks.prompt: Sari's legs hurt when she finally sat down. She ___ in the queue at the bank for over an hour.
blocks.explain: She stood for over an hour, up to a past moment (when she sat down) → had been + -ing. 'has been standing' is up to now, and 'is standing' is about now; the story is in the past.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Sari's legs hurt when she finally sat down. She ___ in the queue at the bank for over an hour.
id.explain: Dia berdiri lebih dari satu jam, sampai suatu saat di masa lalu (waktu dia duduk) → had been + -ing. 'has been standing' untuk sampai sekarang, dan 'is standing' untuk sekarang; ceritanya terjadi di masa lalu.

id.title: had been + -ing: berlangsung sampai suatu saat di masa lalu

material.title: had done or had been doing?

blocks.text:
It's the same choice you made with *I've read* and *I've been reading*, just moved into the past.

**had been + -ing** = the **activity**: how long, or the reason for something you could **see** at that moment:
- *The streets were wet. It **had been raining**.* (the rain had just stopped)
- *Dimas was out of breath because he **had been running**.* (Indonesian *habis lari*)

**had + third form** = the **result**: how many, how much, finished:
- *By noon she **had answered** 40 emails.* (not *had been answering 40 emails*: a number of finished things)

**State verbs** (feelings, knowing, owning: *know, like, believe, understand, have* = own, *be*) stay in the simple form: *I **had known** him for ten years* (not *had been knowing*).

With **live, work, study, teach** + for/since, both forms are fine: *She had lived / had been living there for years.*

id.text:
Ini pilihan yang sama seperti *I've read* dan *I've been reading*, hanya dipindah ke masa lalu.

**had been + -ing** = **kegiatannya**: berapa lama, atau alasan untuk sesuatu yang **terlihat** pada saat itu:
- *The streets were wet. It **had been raining**.* (hujannya baru berhenti)
- *Dimas was out of breath because he **had been running**.* (*habis lari*)

**had + bentuk ketiga** = **hasilnya**: berapa banyak, sudah selesai:
- *By noon she **had answered** 40 emails.* (bukan *had been answering 40 emails*: jumlah hal yang sudah selesai)

**Kata kerja keadaan** (perasaan, pengetahuan, kepemilikan: *know, like, believe, understand, have* = punya, *be*) tetap memakai bentuk simple: *I **had known** him for ten years* (bukan *had been knowing*).

Dengan **live, work, study, teach** + for/since, kedua bentuk benar: *She had lived / had been living there for years.*

rows.en: The streets were wet. It had been raining.
rows.id: Jalanannya basah. Habis hujan.
rows.note: a result you could see → had been + -ing

rows.en: Dimas was out of breath because he had been running.
rows.id: Dimas terengah-engah karena habis lari.

rows.id: Sampai jam 12 siang dia sudah membalas 40 email.

rows.en: I had known him for ten years.

rows.note: know is a state verb → simple

id.note: know adalah kata kerja keadaan → simple

blocks.text: Not sure? Ask: **am I counting something finished, or describing an activity that went on?** Counting (40 emails, six cities, three cups) → **had + third form**. An activity going on, or its traces (wet streets, dirty hands, tired eyes) → **had been + -ing**.

id.text: Ragu? Tanyakan: **apakah aku menghitung sesuatu yang sudah selesai, atau menggambarkan kegiatan yang berlangsung?** Menghitung (40 email, enam kota, tiga gelas) → **had + bentuk ketiga**. Kegiatan yang berlangsung, atau bekasnya (jalan basah, tangan kotor, mata lelah) → **had been + -ing**.

blocks.prompt: By the time the stall closed, Pak Hasan ___ 300 bowls of bakso.
blocks.explain: 300 bowls is a number of finished sales → had + third form: had sold. had been selling is for the activity and how long, not for a number.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: By the time the stall closed, Pak Hasan ___ 300 bowls of bakso.
id.explain: 300 mangkuk adalah jumlah penjualan yang sudah selesai → had + bentuk ketiga: had sold. had been selling untuk kegiatannya dan berapa lama, bukan untuk jumlah.

id.title: had done atau had been doing?

material.title: would and used to: old habits

blocks.text:
You know **used to** + base verb for things that were true in the past but aren't now: habits (*I used to take the KRL*) **and** states (*We used to live in Bogor. I used to have long hair*).

In stories about the past, English also uses **would** + base verb for **repeated actions**, things you did again and again:
*When I was a kid, my dad **would take** me to the market every Sunday. We**'d** **buy** kue cubit and **watch** the birds.*

Three rules for this **would**:
- **Only actions**, never states. With *have, live, like, know, be*, use **used to** (or the past simple): *I would have a bike* ✗ → *I **used to have** a bike* ✓.
- **Set the time first.** On its own, *My dad would take me to the market* sounds like 'he would, if …'. Start with *When I was a kid …* or *Every Sunday …*, or open with **used to**, then continue with **would**.
- **Not for one event**: *Last year I went to Bali* (past simple). And for negatives and questions about habits, use *didn't use to* / *Did you use to …?*

The past simple is always correct too: *When I was a kid, I **had** a bike. Every Sunday my dad **took** me to the market.*

id.text:
Kamu sudah kenal **used to** + kata kerja dasar untuk hal yang dulu benar tapi sekarang tidak lagi: kebiasaan (*I used to take the KRL*) **dan** keadaan (*We used to live in Bogor. I used to have long hair*).

Dalam cerita tentang masa lalu, bahasa Inggris juga memakai **would** + kata kerja dasar untuk **kegiatan yang berulang**, hal yang kamu lakukan lagi dan lagi:
*When I was a kid, my dad **would take** me to the market every Sunday. We**'d** **buy** kue cubit and **watch** the birds.*

Tiga aturan untuk **would** ini:
- **Hanya kegiatan**, tidak pernah keadaan. Dengan *have, live, like, know, be*, pakai **used to** (atau past simple): *I would have a bike* ✗ → *I **used to have** a bike* ✓.
- **Sebutkan waktunya dulu.** Kalau berdiri sendiri, *My dad would take me to the market* terdengar seperti 'dia akan …, kalau …'. Mulailah dengan *When I was a kid …* atau *Every Sunday …*, atau buka dengan **used to**, lalu lanjutkan dengan **would**.
- **Bukan untuk satu kejadian**: *Last year I went to Bali* (past simple). Untuk kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan tentang kebiasaan, pakai *didn't use to* / *Did you use to …?*

Past simple juga selalu benar: *When I was a kid, I **had** a bike. Every Sunday my dad **took** me to the market.*

rows.en: We used to live in a small house near the rice fields.
rows.id: Dulu kami tinggal di rumah kecil dekat sawah.
rows.note: live is a state → used to, not would

id.note: live adalah keadaan → used to, bukan would

rows.en: Every evening, my grandmother would tell us stories.
rows.id: Setiap malam, nenek dulu biasa mendongeng untuk kami.
rows.note: a repeated action, time set first → would is fine

id.note: kegiatan berulang, waktu disebut dulu → would boleh

rows.en: I used to love her nasi uduk.
rows.id: Dulu saya suka sekali nasi uduk buatannya.
rows.note: love is a feeling (state) → used to

rows.en: After school, we'd play football until it got dark.
rows.id: Sepulang sekolah, kami dulu biasa main bola sampai gelap.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: you learnt **would** as *akan* or *mau* (*I'd like*, *If I had time, I would …*). In a memory story, after the time is set, **would** means *dulu biasanya*. And watch **'d**: before a base verb it's **would** (*we'd play*); before a third form it's **had** (*we'd played*).

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: kamu belajar **would** sebagai *akan* atau *mau* (*I'd like*, *If I had time, I would …*). Dalam cerita kenangan, setelah waktunya disebut, **would** berarti *dulu biasanya*. Perhatikan juga **'d**: sebelum kata kerja dasar artinya **would** (*we'd play*); sebelum bentuk ketiga artinya **had** (*we'd played*).

blocks.prompt: When I was at school, I ___ really long hair.
blocks.explain: have long hair is a state (how you looked), not a repeated action → used to have. would is only for repeated actions.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: When I was at school, I ___ really long hair.
id.explain: have long hair adalah keadaan (penampilanmu), bukan kegiatan yang berulang → used to have. would hanya untuk kegiatan yang berulang.

id.intro: Selamat datang di B2! Kamu sudah bisa bercerita dengan past simple, past continuous dan past perfect. Sekarang kamu belajar memilih setiap tense dengan sengaja, menambahkan past perfect continuous (I had been waiting for two hours when she finally arrived), dan bercerita tentang kebiasaan lama dengan would dan used to.
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana memilih antara 'was leaving', 'left' dan 'had left'?
Apa bedanya 'I was waiting' dan 'I had been waiting'?
Kapan saya boleh memakai 'would' sebagai ganti 'used to'?
Apakah 'I had waited for two hours' salah?

assessment.nar-2: Satu kata kerja di kalimat terakhir memakai tense yang salah. Tulis kalimat terakhir yang sudah diperbaiki: It was a busy Monday morning. Everyone was rushing to the lifts. When I got to my desk, I saw that someone already took my chair.

assessment.nar-6: Perbaiki kesalahannya: When we lived in Medan, my father would have a small coffee shop near the market.
